newsitem.title: USA: Viacom, MCA seek more time to settle TV dispute.
newsitem.headline: Viacom, MCA seek more time to settle TV dispute.

text.p: Entertainment giants Viacom Inc. and Seagram Co. Ltd.'s MCA Inc. Wednesday asked a court to give them more time to settle a dispute over their jointly-owned cable network.

Viacom, which owns Paramount Pictures, MTV and Nickelodeon, and Seagram, which owns entertainment and theme park concern MCA Inc., have been fighting for control of their cable channel USA Network, with each side accusing the other of violating the terms of the partnership agreement.
On Monday, testimony was suspended until Thursday to give both sides an opportunity to reach a settlement.
On Wednesday, the companies asked the court to extend the deadline to next Monday.
According to people familar with the talks, the request was not a sign that negotiations had soured but rather that both sides needed more time to reach an agreement.
"It's just taking more time," one source said.

According to published reports, Viacom and MCA are discussing a plan in which Viacom would receive MCA's half of the USA Network in return for Viacom's half of the Sci-Fi cable channel and a substantial cash settlement.

If accepted, the deal would give Viacom sole ownership of the USA cable network, which broadcasts a variety of programmes ranging from re-runs of "Murder, She Wrote" to original movies and the U.S. Open tennis tournament.
In return, MCA would get the less popular Sci-Fi channel, famous for broadcasting re-runs of "Lost in Space" and The Twilight Zone."

Seagram filed suit against Viacom in April, charging the company with violating the terms of the partnership agreement by launching a new cable channel called "Nick at Nite TV Land." Seagram said the partnership prevents either company from operating or launching entertainment cable networks outside of the USA Network.
However, Viacom contends there is no breach of the partnership, that the partnership is working well and that MCA is trying to get control of USA Network "at an unfairly low price."
